Surah Sad [Meccan; it has 86 or 88 verses; it was revealed after Surah al-Qamar]

﴿Sad﴾ God knows best what He means by it. ﴿By the Qur'an, full of reminder﴾ i.e., full of clarification (bayan), or of honour (sharaf). The response to this oath is omitted, i.e., the matter is not as the disbelievers of Mecca say, regarding the multiplicity of gods.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 38, verse 2:

﴿Nay, but those who disbelieve﴾ from among the people of Makkah, ﴿are in arrogance﴾ (ḥamiyya, i.e. zeal and pride) and haughtiness towards faith, ﴿and opposition﴾ (khilaf, i.e. disagreement and enmity) towards the Prophet (ﷺ).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 38, verse 3:

﴿How many﴾ (kam): meaning many. ﴿We destroyed before them many a generation﴾ (qarn): meaning a community (umma) from the past nations. ﴿Then they cried out﴾ (fa-nadaw): when the punishment came down upon them. ﴿But it was not a time for escape﴾ (wa-la tahīn manāṣ): meaning the time was not a time of flight. The ta' in "tahīn" is extra (za'ida), and the clause is a circumstantial state (hal) referring to the subject of "nadaw," meaning: they cried for help while there was no way of escape and no refuge. And the disbelievers of Makkah did not take warning from them.

And they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves (﷾ rasūl min anfusihim, a messenger from among themselves), who warns them and frightens them of the Fire after the Resurrection, and he is the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿And the disbelievers say﴾ — the apparent noun (al-kāfirūn) has been placed in the position of the pronoun (al-muḍmar, the implicit form), [i.e., "they say"].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 5:

﴿Has he made the gods into one God?﴾ When he said to them, "Say: There is no god but Allah." That is, how can one God suffice for all creation? ﴿Indeed, this is an astonishing thing.﴾ That is, a wondrous thing.

And the chiefs among them went off, (saying): "Walk on, and be steadfast in your gods. This is indeed a thing that is intended" against us.

[Their going off was] from their gathering at the house of Abu Talib, and their hearing from the Prophet (ﷺ) in it: "Say: There is no god but Allah." ﴿That walk on﴾: some of them said to others, "Walk on." ﴿And be steadfast in your gods﴾: persist in worshipping them. ﴿Indeed this﴾: what has been mentioned of the monotheism [of the Prophet] ﴿is a thing that is intended﴾ against us.
"We have not heard of this in the latter religion" — that is, the religion of Isa (Jesus) — "this is nothing but a fabrication" — that is, a lie.

Is the Reminder (al-dhikr) sent down to him, of all of us? ﴾ Hmm, let me translate properly.

**"Has the Reminder been sent down upon him from among us?"** The first hamza of ﴿أأُنْزِلَ﴾ may be pronounced with both hamzas fully articulated, or with the second softened (tas-hil), and an alif may be inserted between them in either of these two ways, or omitted; all of these are permitted in recitation. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ means upon him, namely Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿الذِّكْر﴾ means the Qur'an. ﴿مِن بَيْننا﴾ means from among us, and not from the greatest or most noble of us. That is, the Reminder was not sent down to him. ﴿بَلْ هُمْ فِي شَكّ مِن ذِكْرِي﴾ means "Rather, they are in doubt about My Reminder," that is, My revelation, the Qur'an, since they denied the one who brought it. ﴿بَلْ لَمّا﴾ means "Rather, when" they have not yet tasted ﴿عَذاب﴾ the punishment. Had they tasted it, they would have believed the Prophet (ﷺ) in what he brought, and belief would not benefit them at that time.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 9:

﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord's mercy, the Mighty,﴾ the Overpowering, ﴿the Bestower?﴾ The Bestower of prophethood and other things, so that they could give it to whomever they wish.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 10:

﴿Or do they have dominion over the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them?﴾ (If they claim that), ﴿then let them ascend by the means﴾ (al-asbab), the ways leading to the heaven, ﴿and bring down revelation, and single out whomever they wish with it.﴾ And "am" (or) in both places has the meaning of the interrogative hamza of denial (hamzat al-inkar).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 38, verse 11:

﴿Jund ma﴾: that is, they are a contemptible host. ﴿Hunalika﴾: there, in their denial of you. ﴿Mahzum﴾ (defeated): an adjective of ﴿jund﴾. ﴿Min al-ahzab﴾ (of the confederates): also an adjective of ﴿jund﴾; that is, they are like the troops from the kind of the confederates who banded together against the prophets before you. Those were overpowered and destroyed, so likewise We shall destroy these.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 12:

﴿Before them the people of Nuh denied﴾. The feminine form of the verb, *kadhdhabat* (كَذَّبَتْ), is in agreement with the meaning of *qawm* (people), not its grammatical gender (ta'nīth: feminine form). ﴿And ʿĀd and Pharaoh, the Lord of the Stakes﴾. He would have four stakes driven into the ground for anyone with whom he became angry, and he would tie that person's hands and feet to them and torture him.
And Thamud, and the people of Lot, and the companions of the Thicket (al-Aykah), that is, the thicket, and they were the people of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him.

﴿In﴾ meaning "not": ﴿each﴾ of the factions ﴿did not but deny the messengers﴾, because when they denied one of them, they had denied all of them, since their call was one and the same, which is the call to monotheism (tawhid). ﴿So there was due﴾ meaning "it was due," i.e., it became binding (wajaba).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 15:

﴿And they are not awaiting﴾ (yantadhir) ﴿these﴾, i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿except a single shout﴾, which is the blast of the Resurrection, that will descend upon them as punishment, ﴿no respite for it﴾ (fawaq), with the fa' pronounced with a fatha or a damma, meaning: return.

﴿And they said﴾ when there was revealed ﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand﴾ and so on: ﴿Our Lord, hasten to us our qiṭṭ﴾ that is, the record of our deeds, ﴿before the Day of Reckoning﴾. They said that in mockery.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 17:

﴿Be patient over what they say, and remember Our servant Dawud (David), the one of strength.﴾ That is, the strength in worship. He would fast one day and break his fast the next day, and he would stand in prayer for half the night, sleep for a third of it, and stand in prayer for a sixth of it. ﴿Indeed, he was one who constantly turned back (to Allah).﴾ Returning frequently to the good pleasure of Allah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 18:

﴿Indeed, We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] along with him﴾ glorifying with his glorification, ﴿in the evening﴾ at the time of the ʿIshāʾ prayer, ﴿and at sunrise﴾ at the time of the Ḍuḥā prayer, which is when the sun rises and its light becomes full.

And [We subjected] the birds, gathered together [to him]: the birds were gathered to him, glorifying [God] along with him. Each [of the mountains and the birds] was [ever] turning back [to obedience] to Him (lahu awwab), returning to His obedience through glorification.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 20:

﴿And We strengthened his kingdom﴾ We made it strong with the guard and the soldiers, and he had thirty thousand men guarding his sanctuary (mihrab) every night. ﴿And We gave him wisdom﴾ prophethood and correctness in matters. ﴿And decisive speech﴾ clear, sufficient explanation in every purpose.

﴿Wa-hal﴾ (And has...?): The interrogative here carries the sense of wonder and of arousing eagerness to hear what follows (istifham, interrogation; here, a rhetorical device). ﴿Atāka﴾ (has it reached you), O Muhammad, ﴿nabaʾ al-khaṣm﴾ (the news of the litigants), ﴿idh tasawwarū al-miḥrāb﴾ (when they climbed over the prayer chamber). The mihrab of Dawud (Dawud, David): that is, his place of worship, where they were prevented from entering through the door because he was occupied with worship. That is, their news and their story.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 22:

﴿When they entered upon Dawud, and he was alarmed at them, they said: Do not fear. We are two disputants﴾ we are two disputants. It was said: "a group of disputants," to agree with the plural pronoun in what precedes it (namely, the pronoun in ﴿they﴾). It was also said: "two," and the pronoun is according to their meaning. The word khasm (disputant, adversary) is applied to one or more. They were two angels who came in the form of two disputants. What they mentioned happened to them by way of supposition, in order to alert Dawud, peace be upon him, to what had occurred from him: he had ninety-nine wives, and a man had only one woman, and he sought her and married her and consummated the marriage. ﴿One of us has wronged the other, so judge between us with truth and do not exceed the bounds﴾ do not deviate (tajur, do not be unjust) ﴿and guide us﴾ direct us ﴿to the even path﴾ the middle of the way, the right course.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 23:

﴿Indeed, this is my brother﴾, i.e., in my religion. ﴿He has ninety-nine ewes﴾, by which a woman is expressed. ﴿And I have one ewe﴾ ﴿so he said, "Entrust her to me"﴾, i.e., make me her guardian. ﴿And he overpowered me﴾, i.e., overcame me ﴿in speech﴾, i.e., in argument. And the other acknowledged that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 38, verse 24:

﴿He said: "He has certainly wronged you by demanding your ewe be added to his ewes. Indeed, many associates (al-khulata', partners) oppress one another, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and few are they."﴾ *Li-yadummaha* (so that he might add it) *ila ni'ajihi* (to his ewes). *Wa-inna kathiran mina al-khulata'* (and indeed many of the partners) *al-shurakaʾ* (the associates) *li-yabghiya ba'duhum ʿala ba'd* (oppress one another) *illa alladhina amanu wa-ʿamilu al-salihat* (except those who believed and did righteous deeds) *wa-qalilun ma hum* (and few are they). Here *ma* is for emphasising the fewness (*li-ta'kid al-qilla*). Then the two angels, ascending to the heaven in their two forms, said: the man has passed judgement against himself, and Dawud became aware. ﴿And Dawud thought⌋ *ayy ayqana* (i.e., became certain) ﴿that We had only tested him⌋ *awqa'nahu fi fitna* (We had put him into a trial), *ayy baliyya* (i.e., a calamity) *bi-mahabbatihi tilka al-mar'a* (through his love for that woman). ﴿So he sought forgiveness from his Lord and fell down bowing⌋ *ayy sajidan* (i.e., prostrating).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 25:

﴿So We forgave him that; and indeed for him with Us is nearness and a good return.﴾ That is, an increase of good in this world, ﴿and a good return﴾, a return in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 26:

﴿O Dawud, indeed We have made you a khalifa (successor/vicegerent) upon the earth﴾, i.e., manage the affairs of the people; ﴿so judge between the people with truth and do not follow [your] desire﴾, i.e., the desire of the self, ﴿lest it lead you astray from the way of Allah﴾, i.e., from the proofs indicating His oneness. ﴿Indeed, those who go astray from the way of Allah﴾, i.e., from faith in Allah, ﴿will have a severe punishment for having forgotten the Day of Reckoning﴾, i.e., for their forgetting it, ﴿the Day of Reckoning﴾, the abandonment of faith being consequent upon it. Had they been certain of the Day of Reckoning, they would have believed in this world.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 27:

﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain﴾ (ʿabathan, without purpose). ﴿That﴾ means: He created what has been mentioned not for any purpose. ﴿Is the assumption of those who disbelieve﴾ from among the people of Makkah. ﴿So woe﴾ is a valley (wād) [in Hell].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 28:

﴿Shall We make those who believe and do righteous deeds like the corrupters in the earth? Or shall We make the God-fearing like the wicked?﴾ It was revealed when the disbelievers of Makkah said to the believers: "We will be given in the Hereafter the same as what you are given." And "am" (أمْ) here carries the meaning of the interrogative hamza of denial (hamzat al-inkar).

Book (kitāb): a predicate (khabar) of an omitted subject (mubtada'), i.e., this is a book ﴿We have sent down to you, blessed,﴾ that they may ponder (liyaddabbarū): its original form is yatadabbarū, and the tā' was assimilated into the dāl ﴿its verses,﴾ that they may ponder its verses, i.e., look into their meanings, and thus believe. ﴿And that those of understanding may take heed﴾ (yatta'iẓ), ﴿those endowed with minds﴾ (ūlū al-albāb), i.e., people of intellect.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 30:

﴿And We bestowed upon Dawud (David) Sulayman (Solomon)﴾ his son ﴿- how excellent a servant! Indeed, he was ever turning back (to Allah)﴾ i.e., Sulayman. ﴿Indeed, he was awwab﴾ returning (to Allah) often in glorification (tasbih) and remembrance (dhikr) at all times.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 31:

﴿When there were displayed before him, at evening,﴾ — this is what comes after the decline of the sun (al-zawal). ﴿the swift-footed steeds (al-sāfināt)﴾ — al-khayl (horses), the plural of sāfina, which is the one standing on three legs while the other rests on the edge of its hoof; it derives from ṣafana, yaṣfinu, ṣufūnan. ﴿al-jiyād (the fine chargers)﴾ — the plural of jawād, which is the swift one. The meaning is that when they are made to halt, they remain still, and when they gallop, they outstrip. There were a thousand horses displayed before him after he had prayed the noon prayer, because he intended to wage jihad against an enemy on them. So when the display reached nine hundred of them, the sun set, and he had not prayed the afternoon prayer, and so he was distressed.

[He said, "Indeed I have loved"] i.e., I preferred, [the love of the good] i.e., the horses, [over the remembrance of my Lord] i.e., the afternoon prayer (ṣalāt al-ʿAṣr), [until it disappeared] i.e., the sun, [behind the veil] i.e., it hid itself behind that which screens it from sight.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 33:

﴿Bring them back to me﴾, i.e., the horses displayed before him, so they were brought back. ﴿Then he began to pass his hand over﴾ them with the sword, ﴿over the shins﴾, the plural of sāq (shin), ﴿and the necks﴾, i.e., he slaughtered them and cut off their legs, drawing near to God Most High, since he had been occupied with them to the neglect of the prayer, and he gave their flesh in charity. God then compensated him with something better than them and swifter, namely the wind, which runs by his command wherever he wills.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 34:

﴿And We did indeed test Solomon﴾ We tried him by taking away his kingdom. This was because of his marrying a woman whom he loved, who used to worship an idol in his house without his knowledge. His kingdom lay in his ring. He removed it once, at the time he wished to relieve himself, and placed it with his wife named al-Amina, as was his custom. A jinn came to her in the form of Solomon and took it from her. ﴿And We cast upon his throne a body﴾ It was that jinn, and it was Sakhr or someone else, who sat on Solomon's throne; the birds and others gathered around it. Solomon came out in a state other than his own, saw him on his throne, and said to the people, "I am Solomon," but they rejected him. ﴿Then he turned back in repentance﴾ Solomon returned to his kingdom after some days, by reaching the ring, so he put it on and sat on his throne.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 35:

﴿He said, "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that will not belong to anyone after me."﴾ That is, it should not be (for anyone) ﴿after me﴾, meaning other than myself, like His saying ﴿so who can guide him after Allah?﴾, meaning other than Allah.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 36:

﴿So We subjected to him the wind, running gently by his command, wherever he directed﴾ gentle (layyina) ﴿wherever he directed﴾ intended

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 37:

﴿And the devils, every builder﴾ who builds wondrous structures, ﴿and diver﴾ in the sea who extracts pearls.
And others of them, ﴿bound together﴾ [muqarranin], tied up ﴿in shackles﴾ [al-asfad], the fetters, with their hands gathered up to their necks.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 39:

﴿This is Our gift, so bestow or withhold without account.﴾ Give from it to whomever you wish, ﴿or withhold﴾ from giving, ﴿without account﴾, i.e., there is no reckoning against you in that.
﴿And indeed, for him with Us is nearness and a good return.﴾ A similar (statement) has preceded.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 41:

﴿And mention Our servant Ayyub (Job), when he called upon his Lord, [saying] that﴾, that is, [saying] that, ﴿Satan has touched me with distress﴾, meaning harm, ﴿and torment﴾, meaning pain. He attributed this to Satan, although all things are from God, out of courtesy (adab) toward Him, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 42:

﴿Strike﴾ (i.e., strike) ﴿with your foot﴾ (i.e., strike the earth with your foot), so he struck, and a spring of water gushed forth, and it was said: ﴿This is a cool bath and a drink﴾ (water to bathe in and to drink from). So he bathed and drank, and every ailment that was within him and upon him departed from him.

And We gave him his family and the like of them along with them (ووَهَبْنا لَهُ أهْله ومِثْلهمْ مَعَهُمْ), that is, Allah brought back to life for him those of his children who had died and gave him the like of them. "A mercy" (رَحْمَة) — a blessing — "from Us, and a reminder" (وذِكْرى) — an admonition — "for people of understanding" (لِأُولِي الأَلْباب), that is, for those possessed of intellects.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 44:

﴿And take in your hand a bundle (ḍigth) of grass or twigs, and strike with it,﴾ — it is a bundle of grass or of rods — ﴿strike with it⦆ your wife, for he had sworn that he would strike her one hundred blows because she had been slow to come to him one day. ﴿And do not break your oath⦆ by not striking her. So he took a hundred stalks of izkhir (a fragrant grass) or something else, and struck her with them in a single blow. ﴿Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant⦆ — Ayyub. ﴿Indeed, he was ever oft-returning⦆ — turning back to Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 45:

﴿And remember Our servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, owners of strength and vision.﴾ [Ulu al-aydi] those of strength in worship, ﴿wal-absar﴾ [and vision]: insight in the religion. And in another reading, "Our servant" (ʿabdanā) and Abraham is an explanatory apposition to it, and what follows it is conjoined to "Our servant" (ʿabdanā).

Indeed, We made them pure through a pure quality, which is ﴿the remembrance of the Abode﴾, i.e., remembering it and working for it. In another reading it is recited with the genitive construction (idafa), and it is then for explanation (bayan).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 47:

﴿And indeed they are with Us, among the chosen ones﴾ the selected ones, ﴿the excellent﴾. It is the plural of khayyir (خَيِّر), with the letter yaa' shaddah (doubled).

﴿And remember Isma'il and al-Yasa'﴾. He is a prophet, and the lam (اللّام) in the name is superfluous (za'ida), meaning it has no grammatical function. ﴿And Dhu al-Kifl﴾. His prophethood is disputed. It is said that he took responsibility (kafala) for a hundred prophets who fled to him from being killed. ﴿And all of them﴾, meaning all of them together, ﴿are among the good ones﴾. The word الأَخْيار (al-akhyar) is the plural of خَيِّر (khayyir), pronounced with the doubled letter (بِالتَّثْقِيلِ, bi-l-taqil), the emphatic form.

This is a remembrance. That is, this is a mention of them, with fine praise here. ﴿And indeed, for the God-fearing (al-muttaqin)﴾ who include them ﴿is an excellent final return﴾, a place of return in the Hereafter.

Gardens of Eden (jannāt ʿadn) in apposition (badal) or as an explanatory apposition (ʿaṭf bayān) to "a good place of return" (ḥusn maʾāb). "Their doors opened for them" (mufattaḥatan lahumu al-abwāb): the doors of the gardens are opened for them.
[Verse 38:51] ﴿Reclining therein﴾ upon couches.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 52:

﴿And with them will be maidens restraining their gaze, [devoted] to their husbands, of equal age﴾ restraining their eyes upon their husbands, ﴿of equal age﴾ their ages being one, and they are maidens of thirty-three years, plural of "tarb" (peer, of the same age).

This is what you are promised (هَذا مَا تُوعَدُونَ), with the mention shifting from the third person (تُوعَدُونَ read as "they are promised" in the absent form) to the second person (the address form), an iltifat (shift of grammatical person), for the Day of Reckoning (لِيَوْمِ الحِسَاب), meaning: for its sake.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 54:

﴿Indeed, this is Our provision, which has no end.﴾ Meaning: no cessation. The clause (jumla) is either a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of "Our provision," or a second predicate (khabar thani) of "inna" (indeed), meaning: everlasting, or permanent.
﴿This﴾, the aforementioned, is for the believers.

Hell, which they will enter (yaslawnaha): yadkhulūnahā. ﴿And wretched is the resting-place﴾: al-firāsh (the bedding).

This is the commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 57:

﴿This﴾, i.e., the punishment understood from what follows it. ﴿So let them taste it: scalding water and ghasaq﴾: ﴿scalding water﴾, i.e., hot water that burns. ﴿Ghasaq﴾, with a light or a heavy pronunciation (al-takhfif wa al-tashdid): that which flows from the pus of the people of the Fire.

And other punishments of similar kind (﴿وآخَر﴾, read with the plural and the singular), ﴿of its kind﴾, i.e., like what was mentioned of the boiling water (al-hamim) and the dark, pus-like liquid (al-ghassaq), ﴿in pairs﴾, i.e., in varieties; that is, their punishment is of various different kinds.

It is said to them, when they enter the Fire, along with their followers: ﴿This is a host rushing in with you﴾, a host (jam') entering (muqtahim) with you (dakhil maʿakum), that is, entering the Fire with you by force. Then the followers will say: ﴿No welcome for them!﴾, that is, there is no spaciousness for them.
﴿They said﴾ i.e., the followers, ﴿Rather, you! There is no welcome for you! You brought it upon us﴾ i.e., the disbelief, ﴿so wretched is the abode﴾ for us and for you, the Fire.
They also say: ﴿Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us, increase him in punishment twofold﴾, that is, double his punishment for his disbelief.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 62:

﴿And they will say﴾ i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah, while they are in the Fire, ﴿"What is [the matter] with us that we do not see men whom we used to count﴾ in the world

ۛ"Did we take them as objects of mockery (sukhriyyan), with the sīn read with a damma or a kasra? We used to mock them in the world, and the yā' is for the nisba (attribution): meaning, are they missing from us? Or have our eyes swerved (zāghat), turned away (mālat), from them, so that we do not see them?" They are the poor among the Muslims, such as ʿAmmār, Bilāl, Ṣuhayb and Salmān.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 64:

﴿Indeed, that is truth﴾ — its occurrence is necessary, and it is the mutual disputing of the people of the Fire, ﴿the mutual disputing of the people of the Fire﴾, as has preceded.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 65:

﴿Say﴾ O Muhammad, to the disbelievers of Makkah: ﴿I am but a warner﴾, one who frightens with the Fire, ﴿and there is no god except Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ over His creation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 66:

﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the All-Mighty﴾ the Overpowering over His affair, ﴿the Oft-Forgiving﴾ to His friends.
﴿Say﴾ to them.

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿You turn away from it﴾.

Commentary: "You are turning away from it," i.e., turning away from the Qur'an which I have informed you of and brought to you with things that are not known except through revelation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 69:

﴿I had no knowledge of the Exalted Assembly (al-Mala' al-A'la) when they were disputing﴾, i.e., the angels, ﴿when they were disputing﴾ concerning the matter of Adam, when Exalted is He said: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successive authority (khalifah)﴾, and so on.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on Surah 38, verse 70:

﴿Say, "It is only revealed to me that I am a clear warner"﴾ — ﴿إنْ﴾ (in, "not"/"it is not") + ﴿ما يُوحى إلَيَّ﴾ ("what is revealed to me") + ﴿إلّا أنَّما أنا﴾ ("except that I am") — meaning: أيْ أنِّي (i.e., that I am) ﴿نَذِير مُبِين﴾ (a warner, clear) — بَيِّن الإنْذار (clear in the warning).
﴿When your Lord said to the angels, "I am going to create a human from clay."﴾ He is Adam.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 72:

﴿When I have proportioned him﴾ I have completed him, ﴿and breathed into him of My spirit﴾ I have caused it to flow into him, so he became alive. The attribution of the spirit to Him is an honouring of Adam, and the spirit (al-rūḥ) is a subtle body by which a human being lives through its penetration into him. ﴿Then fall down before him in prostration﴾ a prostration of greeting (taḥiyya) by bowing.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 73:

﴿So the angels prostrated, all of them together.﴾ In it there are two emphatics.

Translation of the passage:

﴿Except Iblis﴾ — he is the father of the jinn. He was among the angels, ﴿he was arrogant and was among the disbelievers﴾ in the knowledge of God, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 75:

﴿Said: "O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My two hands?"﴾ That is, "I undertook its creation Myself," and this is an honouring of Adam, for every created thing is one whose creation God undertook. ﴿Have you become arrogant now?﴾ regarding prostration; this is an interrogative for rebuke. ﴿Or were you among the exalted?﴾ meaning, the arrogant ones, so that you became arrogant regarding prostration because you were of them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 77:

﴿He said: "Get out of it"﴾ i.e., out of Paradise. It was also said: out of the heavens. ﴿for indeed you are accursed﴾ expelled.
﴿And indeed, upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense﴾ *al-jaza'* (the requital)
﴿He said, "My Lord, then reprieve me until the day they are resurrected."﴾ That is, until the day the people are raised.
﴿Until the Day of the appointed time﴾, which is the time of the first blast (al-nafkhah al-ula, the first blowing of the Trumpet).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 83:

﴿Except Your servants among them, the sincere ones﴾ i.e., the believers

﴿He said, "Then the truth, and the truth I say"﴾ Both instances of الحَقّ are read in the accusative (بِنَصْبِهِما), though the first (الأَوَّل) may also be read in the nominative (raf', رَفَعَ). The second (الثّانِي) is in the accusative (naṣb), governed by the verb that follows it (فَنَصَبَهُ بِالفِعْلِ بَعْده). The first is said to be in the accusative by the verb mentioned above (قِيلَ بِالفِعْلِ المَذْكُور), or by way of the verbal noun (عَلى المَصْدَر), meaning: أُحِقّ الحَقّ ("I affirm the truth"). It is also said to be in the accusative after the oath particle has been removed (عَلى نَزْع حَرْف القَسَم), and in the nominative as the subject (mubtada', مُبْتَدَأ) whose predicate (khabar, خبر) is omitted, meaning: فالحَقّ مِنِّي ("so the truth is from me"). It is also said that فالحَقّ قَسَمِي ("so the truth is my oath"), and the response to the oath (jawab al-qasam, جَواب القَسَم) follows.
﴿Surely I shall fill Hell with you﴾ i.e., with your offspring, ﴿and with those of them who follow you﴾ i.e., of mankind.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 86:

﴿Say, "I do not ask you for it any payment﴾ for conveying the message, ﴿and I am not of those who pretend﴾ those who fabricate the Qur'an on my own accord.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 38, verse 87:

﴿It is not﴾ i.e., the Qur'an is not ﴿except a reminder﴾, an admonition, ﴿to the worlds﴾, to mankind, the jinn and the rational beings, excluding the angels.

And you will surely come to know its news (﴿ولَتَعْلَمُنَّ﴾), O disbelievers of Makkah, its report (﴿نَبَأَهُ﴾), the truth of it, after a time (﴿بَعْد حِين﴾), i.e., the Day of Resurrection. "ʿAlima" (عَلِمَ) is here in the sense of "ʿarafa" (عَرَفَ, to recognize), and the lam before it is the lam of an oath, with an implied oath: i.e., by Allah.
